content.title: Water Treatment Plant Replacement
content.summary: The City is planning to replace its water treatment plant, which involves constructing a new pump station and pipelines to transport raw water from the Arvada Reservoir and deliver treated drinking water. Three potential sites for the pump station have been identified, with a decision expected by early summer 2026, and construction could begin as soon as 2027. The selected site for the treatment plant is located west of Highway 93 and W. 64th Parkway, chosen for its cost-effectiveness, operational feasibility, and potential for future expansions.
content.body:
## Pump station and pipeline design

Updated February 2026

As a part of the plant replacement, the City will need to build a new pump station and pipeline to deliver raw water from the Arvada Reservoir to be treated at the new plant. An additional pipeline will be built to deliver treated drinking water from the plant into the distribution system. The pipelines are expected to generally follow W. 64th Parkway and sites southeast of the Arvada Reservoir are being evaluated for the pump station.

There are specific criteria that the pump station location must meet to effectively operate and pump water to the plant. These include:

- Elevation below the Arvada Reservoir
- Outside of the flood inundation and hazard zone
- Appropriate route and distance for pipeline from the pump station to the plant
- Existing City property
- Approximately 90 ft. by 90 ft. (size of the infield of a baseball diamond)

### What's happening now

The City has identified three locations that meet the initial criteria above. The City is hiring a contractor to further evaluate suitable sites in the area southeast of the Arvada Reservoir. The contractor will look for additional sites that may be feasible and complete survey and geotechnical work to determine any fatal flaws with the identified sites. Crews may be on site 1-3 days at each location to complete this work. All sites will be restored.

The sites, in no particular order are:

- Parking lot for Bird’s Nest Disc Golf Course
- Northwest corner of Bird’s Nest Disc Golf Course (near hole 6)
- Northeast section of the West Arvada Dog Park
- Other locations southeast of the Arvada Reservoir (TBD)

Any selected site would not remove an amenity in full but a portion of that amenity. The City team will work with interested community members on possible mitigation and improvements for the selected site. 

### Site selection timeline and next steps

The City expects to have a pump station site selected by early summer, as soon as May to begin design work. Should only one site be deemed feasible, that information will be shared with the community. Should more than one location be identified as suitable, the City will consider community preferences in making the final decision. Additionally, the City will engage with community members who use the amenity at the selected location to determine feasible alternative improvements for the area.

### Construction timeline

The replacement plant is under design. The pump station and pipeline construction may begin as soon as 2027, following site selection and design work. Amenity closures and any improvements would be planned in conjunction with this work. Timelines will be updated with more details as that information becomes available.

## Site selectionaerial map with circle at the new site west of Highway 93 and W 66th Ave

Updated September 2025

The site selected for the replacement water treatment plant is just west of Highway 93 and W. 64th Parkway at 6809 State Highway 93.

### Site selection factors

The final site chosen meets many critical criteria that make it the most cost-effective and operationally feasible option for the long term. The City took great care in selecting a location that provides not only financial and operational advantages today, but also the space and adaptability needed to serve the community for generations to come. Key factors that made this site the preferred choice include:

- Lower potential of groundwater, reducing construction costs and long-term maintenance.
- Property shape that allows for easier construction and efficient site layout.
- Minimal disruption to the natural viewscape in the area.
- Better terrain for construction and operations.
- A property size that provides flexibility for future expansions or new treatment processes as technology and regulations evolve.
- Elevation that enables water to be delivered by gravity to most of the city, increasing resilience with fewer pump stations.

### Next steps

- Property annexation into the City (6+ month process)
- Design, planning, and permitting for construction is ongoing
- Construction is anticipated to begin in late 2026
- Anticipated operational date in 2030

Read the [press release](/1390) for more information.

## Background

The Arvada Water Treatment Plant is one of two water treatment plants that serve Arvada water customers. The plant was built in 1979 and as it nears the end of its useful life, it needs to be replaced. The replacement process is a part of planning for the short and long-term future of water treatment in Arvada. This includes creating a plan for:

- treatment location(s),
- sizing of treatment at each location,
- phasing of construction for future water demand.

## Treatment plant siting study

A study was recently conducted to determine the site of a replacement water treatment plant. As a part of this process, City of Arvada residents and water customers were asked to provide feedback ([view the full engagement report](/DocumentCenter/View/2031)). The project team is incorporating public feedback as a part of the decision making process.

### Community feedback

Over 1,500 people interacted with the online forum and over 150 people provided feedback. Themes from the feedback included:

- cost effectiveness in construction and operation of the new facility
- preservation of open space as much as possible
- ensuring security to continue safely delivering high-quality, reliable water to customers

Several videos about the process are available on the City's YouTube page:

- [Water Treatment Plant replacement process](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DY01ZxGIW88)
- [Background on Arvada treatment plants](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FOFSl0hAw4)
- [Water treatment process overview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0pMFazVyezQ)

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=102)

[Why does Arvada need to replace the Arvada Water Treatment Plant?](#)
:   The Arvada Water Treatment Plant has served the community for decades and is nearing the end of its useful life. To continue delivering high-quality, reliable drinking water, the plant is being replaced with a new facility that can more effectively meet current and future demand, comply with evolving water quality standards, and improve sustainability and resilience.

[How was this site selected?](#)
:   The City evaluated multiple potential sites against criteria including cost, operational efficiency, community impact, viewscapes, and long-term flexibility. The chosen site best met these criteria and supports reliable operations for decades to come.

[What is the project timeline?](#)
:   Design of the new plant is underway. Construction is expected to begin in late 2026. The new facility is anticipated to be operational by 2030.

    This timeline is approximate based on current information but may be changed or delayed due to permitting, materials acquisition, weather, or other unforeseen circumstances.

[How is this project being funded?](#)
:   Funding will come from a combination of:

    - Water customer rate revenues – used to repair and replace aging systems.
    - System Development Charges (SDCs) – paid by developers to add capacity to the system.
    - Debt or loans – repaid over 20–30 years using water rate revenues and SDCs.

    Large projects, including this plant replacement, are typically funded by a mix of these sources. This ensures an equitable model where both current and future customers contribute to projects that serve them.

[How much will the project cost?](#)
:   The total project cost, including property acquisition, design, construction, and necessary infrastructure, is estimated at $325 million. This estimate will be adjusted as the project progresses and more precise information becomes available.

[Will this project increase water rates?](#)
:   Yes, water rates will gradually increase to support the cost of construction of the replacement plant, along with other projects to repair and replace aging water infrastructure throughout Arvada. These increases are carefully structured to minimize impact while ensuring we can deliver safe, clean, and reliable water.

[Will the new plant block the views looking west?](#)
:   Protecting viewscapes was a key factor in site selection. Sites that had a higher potential impact on views scored lower in this category during evaluation. The final site was chosen in part because it is expected to have minimal impact on views, especially considering the existing facilities already visible in the area.

[What will happen to the existing water treatment plant?](#)
:   Once the new plant is operational, the existing facility will be decommissioned. The details for decommissioning are still being determined as there are other facilities and infrastructure at that site that will continue to be in service.

[How is the City planning for the future with this project?](#)
:   The City of Arvada has a long history of planning for the future of our water system, dating back to the 1960s. Today, we continue this forward-looking approach to ensure reliable water supply and funding for necessary repairs and replacement. This planning provides sufficient water supply for all customers now and into the future.

[How can I stay informed about the project?](#)
:   The [project website](http://arvadaco.gov/watertreatment) will be the main source of information. Search [arvadaco.gov](//arvadaco.gov) for water treatment or visit the URL [arvadaco.gov/watertreatment](//arvadaco.gov/watertreatment).

    [Sign up for the City’s bi-weekly e-newsletter](https://www.arvadaco.gov/608/Sign-Up-for-City-Newsletter) for major updates.
